breakfast.name: Menemen (Scrambled Eggs with Peppers and Tomatoes)
breakfast.description: A Turkish breakfast specialty from the town of Menemen, combining soft vegetables with scrambled eggs for a simple yet satisfying meal traditionally served family-style
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat
Dice onions and peppers, add to oil and sauté for 5 minutes until softened
Add diced tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes
Gently crack eggs into pan and slowly scramble with the vegetable mixture
Cook for 4-5 minutes until eggs are just set
Add cheese if desired, season with salt and pepper
Serve hot in the same skillet with crusty bread
breakfast.notes: Menemen should be cooked slowly to keep eggs creamy. The dish is traditionally served in the skillet for family-style sharing
breakfast.fun_fact: Menemen originated in the town of Menemen in Northern Izmir where it is believed to have been invented and remains a beloved traditional Turkish breakfast
alternatives: Use red peppers instead of green
Include kaşar cheese instead of feta
Add fresh herbs like parsley or dill

breakfast.name: Simit (Turkish Sesame Bagel)
breakfast.description: A beloved Turkish street food - a golden sesame-crusted bread with a tender, fluffy interior, sitting between a bagel and soft pretzel
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, salt, and sugar in a bowl
Add warm water and oil, knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic
Cover and let rise for 1-1.5 hours until doubled
Divide dough into 8 portions and shape into balls
Roll each into a thin rope about 12 inches long
Bring ends together to form ring and seal
Mix grape molasses with water for syrup
Pour sesame seeds into shallow bowl
Dip each simit ring into syrup, then roll in sesame seeds
Place on oiled baking sheet and let rise 15-20 minutes
Bake at 400°F for 15-18 minutes, turning every 3-4 minutes
Cool on wire rack and serve with cheese, olives, and Turkish tea
breakfast.notes: Rotating simits while baking ensures even browning. Grape molasses creates authentic flavor
breakfast.fun_fact: Turkish simit may have been invented around 1500s during Ottoman Empire. Today it remains a beloved street food, often eaten for breakfast with fresh vegetables and cheese
alternatives: Dip in zaatar instead of sesame

lunch.name: Döner Kebab (Rotisserie Meat Sandwich)
lunch.description: Turkish rotisserie meat sandwich with thin-sliced cooked meat, vegetables and yogurt sauce in pita. Modern döner developed in Istanbul in 19th century
instructions: Mix ground meat with fat, onion, garlic and spices
In vertical rotisserie (or bake at 400°F for 45 min), cook meat until outer layer browns and crisps
Slice thinly from outside
Serve in pita with vegetables and yogurt sauce
Squeeze lemon over filling
lunch.notes: If no vertical rotisserie, shape mixture into loaf on baking sheet and bake until golden, slicing as it cooks
lunch.fun_fact: Modern döner kebab developed in Istanbul in 19th century, revolutionized by vertical rotisserie cooking. One of most popular lunch sandwiches worldwide
